newsitem.title: USA: New Haven mayor says will seek third term.
newsitem.headline: New Haven mayor says will seek third term.

text.p: Mayor John DeStefano, Jr. said Thursday he will seek a third term in office this year.
Democrat DeStefano, 42, is considered a possible candidate for governor, but most analysts think he will not run for state office until sometime after 1998.
"He's kind of in the second tier of possible candidates (for governor)," said a Hartford-based political analyst.
Bridgeport Mayor Joseph Ganim (D) is among those viewed as a far more likely challenger to Republican Gov. John Rowland next year, the analyst said.
DeStefano was re-elected as mayor in 1995, when he captured 80 percent of the vote.
He is considered one of the state's leading advocates of the need for property tax reform to accomplish economic growth.
Among his achievements, he has achieved four budget surpluses and won a city bond upgrading from Standard & Poor's.
